nodes.prompt: Photorealistic vertical 9:16 photo, the first frame of a video shot, looking like an ordinary frame from a real camera with a normal lens, not a render; true-to-life gentle colors and soft natural contrast; fine natural grain; the far background a touch softer than the foreground. No over-sharpening, no HDR, no CGI look. Image 1 is the empty dining room on Friday night: the shot takes place in exactly this room, same furniture, same light; keep the background exactly as in Image 1. Image 2 is her son's character sheet: use it only for the skin tone of the hands and for the sleeves and rings. Image 3 shows the brochure: use it only for its size and cover. Extreme close-up. The photo shows her son's two hands (deep brown skin, lighter palms, a gold wedding band, the cuffs of his plaid button-down shirt) hold the glossy senior-living brochure, cover facing camera and readable, in a hallway stacked with cardboard moving boxes; his face is out of the frame. The brochure is a glossy senior-living brochure whose cover photo shows smiling seniors at a communal dining table. Every moving box is plain brown cardboard, unprinted and unlabeled, with no brand marks. Every hand has five fingers in natural proportion and a natural grip; each person has exactly two arms and two hands; nothing floats. Look: warm evening light from a small chandelier, soft shadows, warm family-film color. Skin as a real camera sees it from a couple of meters away: natural, with subtle texture and slight unevenness, not retouched, not over-detailed; no airbrushed, waxy or plastic skin. Brown skin true to life: rich, natural undertones with soft highlights on the knuckles and visible detail in the shadows; palms lighter than the backs of the hands; never grey, ashy, washed out, orange or lightened. No subtitles, no captions, no text overlays; the brochure cover lettering "WRENFIELD · SENIOR LIVING" stays.

Photorealistic vertical 9:16 photo, the first frame of a video shot, looking like an ordinary frame from a real camera with a normal lens, not a render; true-to-life gentle colors and soft natural contrast; fine natural grain; the far background a touch softer than the foreground. No over-sharpening, no HDR, no CGI look. Image 1 is the chosen photo of this Friday dinner, taken from the main camera at the foot of the table with everyone in their own chair: edit this photo. Image 2 is the grandmother's character sheet: use it only for her face, skin tone, silver hair, glasses on the chain, jewelry and clothes. Image 3 is her son's character sheet: use it only for his face, skin tone, haircut, beard and clothes. Image 4 is the granddaughter's character sheet: use it only for her face, skin tone, braids, earrings and clothes. Image 5 is the son's wife's character sheet: use it only for her face, skin tone and hair. Image 6 shows the boy's clothes: use it only for his sleeves. Image 7 is the real product photo of the wooden utensils. Keep exactly as in Image 1: the room, the camera position and its direction, the light, the table setting, and every person's face, hair and clothes; everyone who sits stays in their own chair from Image 1, and nobody new appears. Change only the framing, the moment, the actions and the expressions described here. Wide shot. The photo shows the same Friday dinner from the same camera, with the same framing as Image 1: the same people in the same chairs. The grandmother has come around the head of the table and stands beside the granddaughter's chair, setting the potato salad bowl down on the table between the granddaughter and her father, a wooden serving spoon in her other hand; her own chair at the head of the table waits for her; moving boxes stand stacked in the hallway beyond the archway; on the sideboard lies the red-and-white checkered towel with a few wooden utensils on it. The grandmother: a 71-year-old Black American woman with medium-deep brown skin and warm undertones, a round face, short tapered silver-white coily hair, gold-framed reading glasses hanging on a chain at her chest, small gold earrings and a small gold cross. She wears a burgundy sweater, small gold earrings and the same floral cotton apron. Her son: a 46-year-old Black American man with deep brown skin, a low taper fade with a little grey at the temples, a neatly trimmed salt-and-pepper beard, a tense jaw and a gold wedding band. He wears a plaid button-down shirt. The granddaughter: a 19-year-old Black American woman with medium brown skin, long knotless braids gathered in a low ponytail, small gold hoop earrings and a bright, expressive face. She wears a green knit sweater. The son's wife: a 44-year-old Black American woman with light-medium brown skin and natural hair in a neat high bun. She wears a soft rust-orange knit sweater instead of her dinner outfit. The son's youngest child, a 10-year-old Black American boy with medium-deep brown skin: only his small hands and forearms appear, at the edge of the table; his face stays out of the frame. His sleeves belong to a plain blue hoodie. The bowl is a large glass bowl of homemade potato salad (potatoes, chopped egg, celery, relish, a light dusting of paprika on top). The seats never change at this table: the grandmother's own chair stands at the head of the table, against the far wall with the archway and the carved wooden fork and spoon, the sideboard in the corner beside it on the son's wife's side; along the side wall with the framed family photos and the china hutch sit, from the head: her son, then the granddaughter, then the aunt; on the other side, facing them, sit from the head: the son's wife, then the boy, then the uncle; the chair at the foot of the table stays empty. The aunt, the grandmother's younger sister, about 66: a Black American woman with medium-brown skin, a round face and shoulder-length silver-grey natural hair in soft twists; she wears a navy cardigan over a cream blouse. The uncle, the aunt's husband, about 70: a Black American man with deep brown skin, a bald head and a short white beard; he wears a brown V-neck sweater over a collared shirt. Only these seven people are at this dinner: the grandmother, her son, his wife, the granddaughter, the boy, the aunt and the uncle; no other guests, no other children, nobody else in the room. Other dishes on the table, soft: collard greens, candied sweet potatoes and cornbread. On the sideboard, where the gift bags stood at the birthday, lies a red-and-white checkered towel with a few wooden utensils on it, and nothing else. Every moving box is plain brown cardboard, unprinted and unlabeled, with no brand marks. The granddaughter's own water bottle stands on the table just beyond her plate, on the side away from her father, clear of her hands, and nobody touches it: a large light-pink insulated tumbler with a handle, a lid and a straw, plain, with no logo or lettering. ACAWOOD SET: solid deep-brown acacia wood utensils with visible natural grain, each carved from a single piece, matte oiled finish (not glossy, not varnished), a small hanging hole near the end of each handle. Exactly seven utensils in the full set: a ladle, a wok spatula, a slotted spoon, a turner, a serving spoon, a mixing spoon and a small spoon. The utensils keep the exact shape of the real product photo. Lighting match: the wooden utensils are lit by exactly the same light as the rest of the scene: the same direction, color temperature, softness and exposure, with soft highlights on the side facing the main light and matching shade on the far side, a soft contact shadow where they touch the counter, towel or a hand. The same grain, softness and color grade as the rest of the photo, the same perspective, and a realistic size (the ladle about 33 cm long). Use Image 7 only for the shapes, number, grain and color of the wood; ignore its lighting, background and shadows. It must look photographed together in one shot, never pasted in or cut out. Food with the wooden utensils: fresh, bright and appetizing, neatly served; the bowl, plates, pot, counter and table are clean and tidy. Expressions true to this moment: everyone at the table quiet and tense, watching the grandmother; the grandmother composed and determined; nobody smiles; natural and believable, never exaggerated or posed. Every hand has five fingers in natural proportion and a natural grip; each person has exactly two arms and two hands; nothing floats. Everyone's eyes stay off-lens; nobody looks into the camera. Look: warm evening light from a small chandelier, soft shadows, warm family-film color. Skin as a real camera sees it from a couple of meters away: natural, with subtle texture and slight unevenness, not retouched, not over-detailed; no airbrushed, waxy or plastic skin. Brown skin true to life: each person keeps their own skin depth and undertone, with soft natural highlights and visible detail in the shadows; palms lighter than the backs of the hands; never grey, ashy or lightened. Final check: the grandmother is the same woman as in her character sheet, with the same skin tone, silver hair, glasses on the chain and gold jewelry; her son is the same man as in his character sheet, with the same skin tone, haircut and beard; the granddaughter is the same young woman as in her character sheet, with the same skin tone and braids; the son's wife is the same woman as in her character sheet. No subtitles, no captions, no on-screen text.
